title: hws: A Tool for Monitoring Hardware Metrics Across Diverse Vendors: A Case Study on Hyperparameter Optimization Algorithms
problem: Gathering power information and hardware metrics across different vendors (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) in a vendor-independent and portable way is non-trivial. Modern AI workloads require monitoring power consumption and energy efficiency across heterogeneous hardware.
motivation: Energy consumption and associated costs are becoming significant problems in the age of AI where massive computational power is necessary.
method: The authors propose hws, a hardware sampling library for Python and C++ that abstracts vendor-specific APIs to provide unified access to hardware metrics. The library collects power draw, total power consumption, clock frequencies, memory consumption, and utilization rates for CPUs and GPUs from NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel. They validate through a case study analyzing hyperparameter optimization algorithms on neural network architectures and GPU-accelerated SVM implementations.
key_novelty: A vendor-independent and portable hardware monitoring library providing unified access to power and performance metrics across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs and CPUs.
contributions: hws hardware sampling library supporting Python and C++ interfaces
Vendor-independent abstraction layer for power and performance monitoring across heterogeneous hardware
Support for comprehensive metrics including power draw, frequency, memory consumption, and utilization
Case study demonstrating HPO algorithm analysis and characterization

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: power draw and total power consumption
metrics.other: clock frequencies, memory consumption, utilization rates

primary_theme: Cross-vendor hardware power and performance monitoring
